statement: Current distributed benchmark defaults and historical selection retain a retired consensus-provider axis, causing the strict zero-reference audit and unrelated normal landing proofs to fail. The benchmark history owner must select the first usable summary for its existing similarity key without a consensus selector, remove the unused provider-switch defaults, and preserve comparison thresholds, parity/ratio/mitigation policy and report provenance. This repairs the harness gate only; runtime consensus and benchmark execution are unchanged.

constraints.statement: The historical benchmark selection owner is createDistributedRunRuntimeBundle in test/distributed/run-runtime-helpers.js, consumed by test/distributed/run.js. Remove the obsolete axis there and its defaults, rather than add a renamed selector, competing policy or scanner exception.

Retain existing caller report order, exact similarity matching, first positive finite throughput selection, report path/timestamp, throughput regression, PostgreSQL ratio, parity, mitigation and missing-baseline behavior.

The existing strict zero-reference audit is the red/green discriminator. Retain focused real-entry helper tests plus existing runner tests and normal static/landing gates. No distributed cluster or release acceptance is claimed. The probe reads receipts only.
